correctness.rationale: Exact occupancy indicator probabilities prove the general covariance expression; uniform negativity follows from a strict binomial inequality. Rare-collision coupling gives the explicit positive limit and finite error bound. Independent Poisson counts give the negative Poisson covariance. Exact rational sample enumeration and bound checks reproduce the finite cases. No finite experiment is substituted for an infinite proof.

The prior uniform richness–frequency theorem implies the negative uniform-case covariance because, in a uniform alphabet, missing mass is proportional to the number of unoccupied categories. That is a covered substatement and is explicitly not independently claimed.
The Ben-Hamou et al. Poisson covariance calculation implies the negative Poisson substatement; only the fixed-sample positive family and cross-model reversal remain as the independent claim.

value.rationale: Good–Turing singleton frequency is a standard estimator of missing mass; their covariance enters the exact mean-square error decomposition. The result exhibits a genuine, all-sample-size reversal of the estimator–target covariance when replacing a fixed sample with a Poisson sample of matching mean, a meaningful caution for de-Poissonized risk analysis.
